_readme: The Road Here (V1.7 build, October 2026; Phase 3A scaffold): every word on the page, section by section. **text** is set in bold (one phrase a paragraph at most); `accent` is the headline phrase in the accent color. No numbered eyebrows or chapter navigation (V1.7). Images are asset ids in assets.json (road-*). Privacy: the band is never named, linked or described in identifying detail anywhere on this page or in its metadata. The milestones are John's approved labels (V1.7, 30 October 2026).

meta.title: The Road Here
meta.description: Before Web3, John Cowin spent 13 years studying music, performing professionally and running the business behind an internationally distributed music project.

hero.headline: Before Web3, there was music.
hero.copy: Before Web3, I spent **13 years** studying music, performing professionally, and running the business behind an internationally distributed music project. What started behind a drum kit grew into an education in entrepreneurship, marketing, partnerships, creative work, and day-to-day operations.

school.headline: From practice rooms to 140+ shows a year.
paragraphs: I studied **performance and music business**, then put that training to work building an original music project from the ground up.

What began with local shows grew into **more than a decade as a professional musician**, including major festivals, television appearances, live FM-radio performances and interviews, and worldwide distribution through The Orchard, a Sony Music subsidiary.

milestones.label: Live performances per year at peak
Major festivals, television appearances, and live FM radio

operator.headline: On stage at night. Running the business by day.
operator.copy: Before professional management and distribution came on board, I handled **much of the business side myself**. Even after management joined, I stayed on as tour manager.

pivot.headline: Then 2020 happened.
paragraphs: After years of near-constant touring, I was already ready for a life with more time at home. Then COVID brought live music to a stop.

Around the same time, I found DeFi. I studied the technology, joined projects as an investor and community member, and built relationships the same way I had in music: by showing up and contributing. That led to my **first professional role in Web3**.

timeline.what: Years of touring, sometimes 140+ shows a year
Discovering DeFi: studying the technology, investing, joining communities

led.headline: Different industry. Familiar instincts.
led.copy: The work changed. The instincts didn't. Building an audience, promoting a product, running events, and keeping a business moving became **the foundation for the marketing work I do today**.
